family_id: PANTHER:PTHR30589
family_name: PROLIPOPROTEIN DIACYLGLYCERYL TRANSFERASE
preferred_name: Lgt prolipoprotein diacylglyceryl transferase family
summary: Lgt enzymes are polytopic cytoplasmic-membrane transferases that move a diacylglyceryl group
  from phosphatidylglycerol to the lipobox cysteine of translocated prolipoproteins, the first and committed
  step of bacterial lipoprotein maturation. The family is a single bacterial clade, found in diderms (E.
  coli, P. putida) and monoderms (B. subtilis, Staphylococcus, Listeria, Streptococcus) alike, and PANTHER
  defines one subfamily (SF0) that holds all members in the inventory. Lgt is essential in E. coli but
  dispensable in B. subtilis, a difference in the physiological consequence of non-lipidation, not in
  the enzyme's activity.
functional_coherence: COHERENT
coherence_reason: Every PAINT assertion sits at one family-root node (PTN000778741, Bacteria), and the
  three reviewed members spanning Gammaproteobacteria and Firmicutes accept the activity, location and
  process with experimental support in E. coli and B. subtilis. No IRD/IKR loss rows exist and no member
  is known to have lost activity.

interpro/panther/PTHR33695/PTHR33695-rev.text:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR33695
family_name: LIPOPROTEIN SIGNAL PEPTIDASE
preferred_name: LspA signal peptidase II family (peptidase A8)
summary: LspA (signal peptidase II) enzymes are small polytopic cytoplasmic-membrane aspartic proteases
  of the peptidase A8 family that remove the signal peptide from diacylglyceryl-prolipoproteins immediately
  upstream of the lipidated cysteine, the second step of bacterial lipoprotein maturation after Lgt. The
  family is a single bacterial clade present in diderms and monoderms; PANTHER defines one subfamily (SF1)
  holding all members. Two conserved aspartates (Asp-102 and Asp-129 in B. subtilis) are the proposed
  catalytic residues.
functional_coherence: COHERENT
coherence_reason: Both PAINT assertions sit at the family-root node PTN002134743 (Bacteria) with no loss
  rows; E. coli, P. putida and B. subtilis members share the activity, location and process.

interpro/panther/PTHR38686/PTHR38686-rev.text:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR38686
family_name: APOLIPOPROTEIN N-ACYLTRANSFERASE
preferred_name: Lnt apolipoprotein N-acyltransferase family
summary: 'Lnt enzymes are cytoplasmic-membrane N-acyltransferases with a periplasmic nitrilase-like (CN
  hydrolase) catalytic domain. They transfer an acyl chain from a glycerophospholipid to the free amino
  group of the diacylglyceryl cysteine of apolipoproteins, the terminal step of lipoprotein maturation
  in Proteobacteria and other diderms. The family is restricted in phylogenetic range compared with Lgt
  and LspA: the cached member inventory (reviewed UniProt entries) contains no Firmicutes member, B. subtilis included, and actinobacteria carry members fused
  to a Ppm1 polyprenol-phosphate mannose synthase domain (M. tuberculosis O53493). PANTHER defines one
  subfamily (SF1) holding all members.'
functional_coherence: MOSTLY_COHERENT
coherence_reason: All members share the Lnt domain and its N-acyltransferase role, with PAINT CC/BP assertions
  at PTN002214718 seeded by E. coli Lnt. The actinobacterial Ppm1/Lnt fusions add an unrelated glycosyltransferase
  activity, and three PAINT rows in this family's file (glycolipid biosynthesis, dolichyl-phosphate mannosyltransferase,
  N-carbamoylputrescine amidase) come from nodes of other PANTHER families' trees rather than from the
  Lnt clade.

document.summary: Lnt enzymes are cytoplasmic-membrane N-acyltransferases with a periplasmic nitrilase-like (CN hydrolase) catalytic domain. They transfer an acyl chain from a glycerophospholipid to the free amino group of the diacylglyceryl cysteine of apolipoproteins, the terminal step of lipoprotein maturation in Proteobacteria and other diderms. The family is restricted in phylogenetic range compared with Lgt and LspA: the cached member inventory (reviewed UniProt entries) contains no Firmicutes member, B. subtilis included, and actinobacteria carry members fused to a Ppm1 polyprenol-phosphate mannose synthase domain (M. tuberculosis O53493). PANTHER defines one subfamily (SF1) holding all members.
document.coherence_reason: All members share the Lnt domain and its N-acyltransferase role, with PAINT CC/BP assertions at PTN002214718 seeded by E. coli Lnt. The actinobacterial Ppm1/Lnt fusions add an unrelated glycosyltransferase activity, and three PAINT rows in this family's file (glycolipid biosynthesis, dolichyl-phosphate mannosyltransferase, N-carbamoylputrescine amidase) come from nodes of other PANTHER families' trees rather than from the Lnt clade.
